text.en: Raju pushed a door near its hinge and then near its handle. "The handle is easier," he said, and his teacher smiled: "That is the moment of a force."

The turning effect of a force about a fixed point or axis is the moment of the force, or torque, equal to the force multiplied by the perpendicular distance. The principle of moments says that when a body is balanced, the clockwise moment equals the anticlockwise moment. A couple consists of two equal and opposite forces on the same body along different parallel lines. It has a turning effect even though the net force is zero.
Newton's second law says that force is proportional to the rate of change of momentum, which gives F = ma, and a unit force produces an acceleration of 1 m/s^2 in a mass of 1 kg. Impulse equals the change in momentum. For a constant force, it equals force multiplied by time. Newton's third law says every action has an equal and opposite reaction. The principle of conservation of linear momentum says the total momentum of a system stays constant if no external force acts, and the rocket uses it for propulsion.
Newton's universal law of gravitation says every two bodies attract with a force proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them, with G = 6.674 x 10^-11 N m^2 kg^-2. Acceleration due to gravity g changes with height and depth. Mass is the amount of matter and weight is the force of gravity. Apparent weight changes in a lift, and in free fall we feel weightlessness.

A push can start a cart, slow it or change its direction. Pressing on a soft object can instead change its shape.

board.text: Forces can change speed, direction or shape

text.en: Two opposite pushes of eight newtons and five newtons leave a net force of three newtons in the direction of the larger push.
A stopped bus and its passengers start moving. Their bodies tend to stay at rest at first, so they feel as if they lean back.

board.text: Inertia is resistance to change in motion

text.en: When a vehicle turns, your body tends to continue in its old direction. A seat belt helps the vehicle turn your body with it.
Newton’s first law says a body stays at rest or keeps the same velocity when the net force is zero. Moving bodies do not need a force simply to keep moving.
A two-kilogram cart moving right at three metres per second has a momentum of six kilogram metres per second to the right.
If right is positive, a cart moving left has negative velocity and momentum. Keep that convention while adding momenta.
On a door, draw a line along the push. The turning distance is measured from the hinge at right angles to that line.
A ten-newton push can give more torque near the handle than near the hinge. The force is the same, but the perpendicular distance is larger.

board.text: Farther from the pivot gives more turning effect

text.en: On a beam, twenty newtons half a metre from the pivot can balance ten newtons one metre away on the opposite side. Both moments are ten newton metres.
Two hands pushing opposite sides of a steering wheel in opposite directions can turn it. Their forces cancel as pushes, but their moments add.

board.text: A couple turns without a net force

text.en: If an eight-newton force pushes right and two newtons act left, the net is six newtons right. A mass of three kilograms speeds up at two metres per second squared to the right.

board.text: The force in F = ma is the net force

text.en: A net force of one newton on a mass of one kilogram produces an acceleration of one metre per second squared.

board.text: One newton = one kilogram metre per second squared

text.en: A steady ten-newton push for half a second gives an impulse of five newton seconds. The body’s momentum changes by five kilogram metres per second.

board.text: Impulse and momentum have matching units

text.en: When a ball is caught, its momentum falls to zero. Moving the hands back spreads that change over more time and reduces the average force.

board.text: A longer stopping time can reduce average force

text.en: A rower pushes water backwards, and the water pushes the rower and boat forwards. These two forces act on different bodies.

board.text: Third-law forces act on different bodies

text.en: A two-kilogram cart at three metres per second sticks to a stationary one-kilogram cart. If the net external force is negligible, their shared speed is two metres per second.
A rocket pushes exhaust backwards. The exhaust pushes the rocket forwards. This force works even where there is no surrounding air.
Keep two masses the same and double the distance between their centres. The gravitational force becomes one-quarter as large.

board.text: Double the separation: one-quarter of the force

text.en: Your mass in kilograms remains the same at different places. Your weight in newtons depends on the local acceleration due to gravity.

board.text: Mass and weight are different quantities

text.en: A mass of ten kilograms near Earth’s surface has weight about ninety-eight newtons when g is nine point eight metres per second squared.
A floor scale measures the push of the floor on you. In free fall there is no supporting push, even though gravity is still acting.

board.text: Apparent weight is the support force

problem.en: A force of 20 N acts at 0.5 m from the hinge. Find the moment.

text.en: Moment = force x perpendicular distance.
Moment = 10 N m.

problem.en: A 20 N downward force acts 0.50 m left of a pivot. What downward force 1.0 m to the right balances the beam?

text.en: The left-side moment is 20 × 0.50 = 10 N m.

why.en: Multiply the force by the perpendicular distance to the pivot.

text.en: The right force must be 10 N.

why.en: Ten newtons × one metre gives the same moment in the opposite direction.

problem.en: A steady force of 12 N acts rightwards for 0.25 s on a cart. Find the impulse.

text.en: Multiply 12 N by 0.25 s.

why.en: Impulse from a constant force is force times time.

text.en: The impulse is 3 N s to the right.

why.en: Momentum increases by 3 kg m/s towards the right.

problem.en: A 2 kg cart moving right at 3 m/s sticks to a stationary 1 kg trolley. Find their common velocity.

text.en: The total momentum before contact is 2 × 3 = 6 kg m/s to the right.

why.en: The stationary trolley has zero initial momentum.

text.en: Divide 6 kg m/s by the combined mass of 3 kg to get 2 m/s right.

why.en: With negligible external force, total momentum stays the same.

prompt.en: A friend says Mass and weight of a body are the same on the Moon. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Weight depends on g and is less on the Moon.

points.en: Moment equals force times the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the force’s line of action.
Momentum is conserved without external force.
Gravitational force depends on masses and distance.
